en.title: How the 737-300 turned Boeing's small narrowbody into a family
en.summary: In the late 1970s the Boeing 727 dominated Boeing's narrowbody lineup while the 737 was a small narrowbody used like a large regional jet; the 737-300, released in 1984, changed that, turning the 737 into a family and setting up the 737NG.
body: In the late 1970s, the Boeing 737 was not the dominant narrowbody everyone knows today. That was the Boeing 727, a larger, three-engined aircraft used for medium-length flights around the world, while the 737 was Boeing's small narrowbody, essentially used like a large regional jet. As the 727's three-engined layout increasingly became obsolete, burning too much fuel for its size and range, Boeing began studies on a new 737 variant in 1979, and in 1984 released the 737-300. The most noticeable difference was its extended fuselage, increasing passenger capacity and lowering unit costs; the wing was tweaked for better aerodynamics, Boeing swapped out the 1960s-era Pratt & Whitney JT8Ds for the new CFM56-3 high-bypass turbofan, and the plane received a new vertical stabilizer design, while the cabin and flight deck were modernized.

The 737-300 competed mainly against the McDonnell Douglas MD-80, but it was more fuel-efficient while carrying slightly fewer passengers, and it was used by many airlines to replace older 727s. The 757, which debuted in 1983 as a clean-sheet twinjet to succeed the 727, carried more passengers and had superior range and fuel burn, but it was expensive, the US market began shifting towards smaller aircraft, and fuel prices dropped, so many airlines kept their depreciated 727s longer or bought the cheaper MD-80. The 737-300 therefore became a crucial aircraft, smaller and cheaper to buy than the 757. Boeing then stretched the airframe by about three to four rows to create the 737-400, debuting in 1988 with Piedmont Airlines, and shrank the fuselage to create the 737-500, which entered service in 1990 to directly succeed the 737-200. On its own, the 737-300 sold 1,113 examples, with the 737-400 receiving 486 orders and the 737-500 receiving 389, bringing the 737 Classic to 1,988 sales in total, against 1,049 orders for the 757 including the later 757-300 and 1,191 for the MD-80. Airbus, meanwhile, officially launched the clean-sheet single-aisle A320 in 1984, and the A320-100 entered service in 1988 with Air France, introducing a full glass cockpit, digital fly-by-wire controls and sidestick controls; the loss of the United Airlines order to the A320 prompted Boeing to revisit the 737, leading to the 737NG, whose 737-800 succeeded the 737-400 and slightly outsold the A320-200 despite debuting about a decade later.

facts.claim: In the late 1970s, the Boeing 727, a larger three-engined aircraft, dominated as Boeing's narrowbody, while the 737 was Boeing's small narrowbody, used essentially like a large regional jet.

Boeing began studies on a new 737 variant in 1979, and in 1984 released the 737-300, with an extended fuselage, a tweaked wing, CFM56-3 high-bypass turbofans replacing the Pratt & Whitney JT8Ds, a new vertical stabilizer design, and a modernized cabin and flight deck.
The 737-300 competed mainly against the McDonnell Douglas MD-80, was more fuel-efficient while carrying slightly fewer passengers, and was used by many airlines to replace older 727s.

The 757 debuted in 1983 and was larger and more expensive than the 727, while the US market shifted towards smaller aircraft and fuel prices dropped, so many airlines kept their depreciated 727s longer or bought the cheaper MD-80.

Boeing stretched the 737-300 by about three to four rows to create the 737-400, debuting in 1988 with Piedmont Airlines, and shrank the fuselage to create the 737-500, which entered service in 1990 to succeed the 737-200.

Boeing sold 1,113 examples of the 737-300, while the 737-400 received 486 orders and the 737-500 received 389 orders, bringing the 737 Classic to 1,988 sales in total, against 1,049 orders for the 757 including the 757-300 and 1,191 for the MD-80.

Airbus officially launched the clean-sheet single-aisle A320 in 1984, and the A320-100 entered service in 1988 with Air France, introducing a full glass cockpit, digital fly-by-wire controls and sidestick controls.

The loss of the United Airlines order to the A320 prompted Boeing to revisit the 737, leading to the 737NG, with the 737-800 succeeding the 737-400 and slightly outselling the A320-200 despite debuting about a decade later.

zh.title: 拯救波音窄體機隊的737-300：從小型區域機到家族核心
zh.summary: 1970年代末，波音窄體機市場由三引擎727主導，737只是小型窄體機；1984年問世的737-300以加長機身與CFM56-3引擎扭轉局勢，成為737家族化的起點，也為後來的737NG鋪路。
body: 1970年代末，波音窄體機的主角並非737，而是體型較大、三具引擎的727，737當時只是波音的小型窄體機，角色近似大型區域客機。隨著727的三引擎布局因油耗過高而逐漸過時，波音一方面研發全新的雙引擎布局取代727，另一方面也因737-200成功而著手改良737；波音於1979年開始研究新737衍生型，並於1984年推出737-300。737-300機身加長、機翼經過調整，引擎由1960年代的普惠JT8D換裝CFM56-3高涵道比渦扇引擎，垂直尾翼重新設計，客艙與駕駛艙也現代化，整體比已受歡迎的737-200更強大、更省油、更先進。

737-300主要對手是麥道MD-80，雖然載客略少，但燃油效率更佳，許多航空公司用它取代老舊727；同一時期，1983年問世的757雖然載客更多、航程更長，但價格昂貴，且美國市場轉向小型飛機、油價下跌，許多航空公司寧可延長727的使用年限或購買較便宜的MD-80，737-300因此填補了比757更小、更便宜的市場空缺。波音後續再將737-300拉長約三至四排座位，於1988年由皮埃蒙特航空率先引進737-400，並縮短機身推出於1990年投入服務、直接接替737-200的737-500；737-300共售出1113架，737-400獲得486架訂單，737-500獲得389架訂單，737Classic合計達1988架銷售，超越757系列的1049架與MD-80的1191架。歐洲方面，空中巴士於1984年正式推出全新單走道A320，A320-100於1988年隨法國航空投入服務，帶來全玻璃座艙、數位線傳飛控與側桿操縱；美國聯合航空訂單流向A320，更促使波音重新檢視737，進而推出737NG，其中接替737-400的737-800雖然晚了約十年問世，銷量卻略勝A320-200。
